deed: ש"י עגנון היה הסופר העברי הראשון שזכה בפרס נובל לספרות
title: S.Y. Agnon won the 1966 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first Hebrew writer to win it

trailer.text: According to JTA, S.Y. Agnon is Israel's foremost classical writer, who served as a link between the Hebrew literature of his generation and the Hebrew literature of earlier periods.
In 1966 the Israeli Hebrew writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature, for his narrative art with motifs from the life of the Jewish people.
He was the first Israeli to win a Nobel Prize in any field, and he remains the only Hebrew-language author to have received the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Agnon was a deeply devout Jew, and he shared the prize with the Jewish poet Nelly Sachs.
The King of Sweden presented the prize to the two Jewish winners, and Agnon sat at the ceremony wearing a velvet yarmulke.
In Israel, his award was viewed as a major diplomatic achievement.

paragraphs.text: According to the Nobel website, Agnon was born in Buczacz, and he was a native of Galicia.
He was born to an affluent and urbane family.
In the family, traditional Jewish culture and modern European culture existed side by side.
The sources disagree on the year Agnon arrived in the Land of Israel.
In 1908 he published his first story in Eretz Israel, "Agunot", under the pen name Agnon.
Agnon later moved to Germany, and according to the Nobel website he met his wife there.
On 6 June 1924 a fire broke out in his home in Bad Homburg.
All his manuscripts and his book collection were destroyed in the fire.
According to the Nobel website, after the fire the family returned to Palestine.
According to the Jewish Press, his valuable library was destroyed again in the 1929 riots in Jerusalem.
According to the journal AJS Review, published by Cambridge University Press, in October 1912 the Hebrew writer Shmuel Yosef Agnon, aged 24, boarded a ship in the port of Jaffa on his way to Berlin.
Before the Nobel, Agnon twice won the Bialik Prize, in 1934 and in 1950.
He also twice won the Israel Prize for literature, in 1954 and in 1958.
According to Haaretz, Agnon was first put forward as a candidate for the Nobel Prize as early as 1947, but he won the prize only in 1966.
He did not win until 1966.
The wealthy businessman Zalman Schocken was Agnon's supporter and publisher.
Schocken later played a central role in promoting him for the prize.
In the year before the award, most of his works were published by West Germany's Fisher Verlag, and Agnon became more widely known in the world.
According to the report, the publisher also handled the technical aspects of his candidacy.
According to the Jewish Press, Österling worked behind the scenes to deflect political opposition to awarding the literature prize to two Zionist Jews.
At nearly 80, Agnon was much older than the typical Nobel laureate in literature.
According to Rabbi Saks, Agnon was happy to receive the prize he had sought for decades.
Kol Israel radio announced that S.Y. Agnon, the Israeli Hebrew writer, had been awarded the 1966 Nobel Prize in Literature.
The prize citation was "for his profoundly characteristic narrative art with motifs from the life of the Jewish people".
According to JTA, Agnon remained calm when he heard of the award, although he was evidently surprised.
According to Rabbi Saks, Agnon said upon the announcement of the award that the ability to write a single sentence properly in Hebrew is worth all the prizes in the world.
Prime Minister Levi Eshkol sent him his congratulations.
Education Minister Zalman Aranne visited his home.
Agnon became the Jewish state's first Nobel Prize laureate.
According to Rabbi Daniel Bouskila, he was the first Hebrew-language writer to win a Nobel Prize.
The prize was considered a tribute not only to the foremost Hebrew writer, but also to Israeli literature as a whole.
In Israel, the award was seen as an opportunity for the young state to gain attention as a cultural force in the world.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Agnon brought great pride to the State of Israel.
According to Haaretz, the final decision on the award was made on 20 October 1966, and at the end of the meeting Österling announced the winners to the press

According to the Jewish Press, because the ceremony was scheduled for Shabbat Chanukah, it had to be delayed for Agnon, who refused to come before he had said the evening prayer, made Havdalah and lit Chanukah candles.
Agnon saw himself as a representative of the entire Jewish people.
According to Rabbi Bouskila, on 10 December 1966 Shabbat in Stockholm ended at 15:55.
Agnon, his wife and his daughter had 35 minutes left to reach the concert hall.
When Shabbat ended, Agnon prayed the evening Maariv service and made Havdalah for his family.
To save time, he shaved in the limousine on the way to the ceremony.
At the ceremony Agnon sat in formal ceremonial attire, with a velvet yarmulke on his head.
The audience noticed that in place of a top hat he wore a black velvet yarmulke.
According to his daughter, Emunah Yaron, many did not believe that Agnon was an observant Jew.
According to her, a big black kippah always covered his head.
King Gustav VI Adolf of Sweden presented the 1966 Nobel Prize in Literature to two Jewish winners.
Agnon, 78, writes in Hebrew.
Nelly Sachs, 75, writes in German.
Sachs was a Jewish poet and playwright, a German refugee who fled to Sweden.
The two shared a prize of $60,000.
Dividing the literature prize between two winners is not common, although there is precedent for it.
The chairman of the Academy's Nobel Committee said that the purpose of joining the winners was to honor writers who write in different languages but are united in spiritual kinship.
On behalf of the Swedish Academy, Dr. Ingvar Andersson told Agnon that they honor in him "a combination of tradition and prophecy, of saga and wisdom".
Österling praised Agnon for a combination of realism and mysticism.
According to him, Agnon has a strange, fairy-like poetry reminiscent of Chagall's motifs from the Bible.
Agnon opened his remarks by saying that a Jew cannot enjoy a meeting with a king without an appropriate blessing.
He delivered the opening section of the speech in Hebrew.
The full text was read on his behalf in English.
He briefly described his life.
He said that even in his youth in Galicia he had always regarded himself as a Jew from Jerusalem.
According to the Jerusalem Post, he recounted that he wrote his first song at the age of five, out of longing for his father, who was away on business.
He listed his teachers in poetry and literature, first among them the Sacred Scriptures, from which he learned to combine letters.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Agnon said that his heart told him that the Jewish sources he had mentioned were responsible for his award.
At the festive dinner, Agnon was served a specially prepared kosher meal.
It was served on a plate never used before, matching the royal dinnerware.
According to Rabbi Jeffrey Saks, Agnon used the occasion of receiving the prize for an extended discussion with King Gustav.
In May 1967 Agnon set out on a tour of the United States.
Agnon died a few years after receiving the Nobel Prize in Stockholm on 10 December 1966.
He was buried on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem.
Agnon remains Israel's sole literature laureate.
The NIS 50 bill bore his image, alongside an excerpt of his acceptance speech.
His memory lives on in Sderot Shai Agnon in Jerusalem.
It also lives on in a synagogue named after him, near his old home in Talpiot.
In 2007 his work was named among the ten most important works of modern Hebrew literature.
According to Rabbi Saks, Agnon was not happy about the idea of sharing the prize with Sachs.
According to Rabbi Saks, Foreign Minister Abba Eban thought that he ought to have a hand in crafting Agnon's speech.
In Rabbi Saks's words, as a piece of rhetoric the text of the speech is decidedly bizarre.
According to the Jewish Press, much of Agnon's work has become inaccessible even to Hebrew readers in Israel.

disagreements.question: In what year was Agnon born?

versions.says: According to the Nobel Prize website, Agnon was born on 17 July 1888
According to Rabbi Saks, in the historical record Agnon was born in the summer of 1887
According to Rabbi Saks, Agnon himself claimed he was born on Tisha B'Av 1888, and the obfuscation was likely related to efforts to evade the draft

claims.text: לפי JTA, עגנון הוא הסופר הקלאסי הבולט של ישראל, שהיווה חוליית קישור בין הספרות העברית בת דורו לספרות העברית של תקופות קודמות.
claims.quote: Mr. Agnon is Israel’s foremost classical writer who has served as a link between the Hebrew literature of this generation and the vast expanse of Hebrew literature of earlier periods.

claims.text: רדיו קול ישראל הודיע כי ש"י עגנון, הסופר העברי הישראלי, זכה בפרס נובל לספרות לשנת 1966.
claims.quote: Kol Israel radio announced today that S.Y. Agnon, the Israeli Hebrew writer, has been awarded the 1966 Nobel Prize for Literature.

claims.text: נימוק הפרס לעגנון היה: על אמנות הסיפור המאופיינת עמוקות שלו, עם מוטיבים מחיי העם היהודי.
claims.quote: for his profoundly characteristic narrative art with motifs from the life of the Jewish people

claims.text: עגנון היה הישראלי הראשון שזכה בפרס נובל בכל תחום, והוא עדיין הסופר היחיד בשפה העברית שקיבל את פרס נובל לספרות.
claims.quote: Agnon was the first Israeli to win a Nobel in any field, and he remains the only Hebrew-language author ever to have received the Nobel Prize in literature.

claims.text: עגנון, יהודי אדוק מאוד, פתח את דבריו באמירה שיהודי אינו יכול ליהנות מפגישה עם מלך בלי ברכה מתאימה.
claims.quote: Mr. Agnon, who is a deeply devout Jew, opened his remarks by noting that a Jew could not enjoy an occasion of meeting a king without an appropriate blessing.

claims.text: עגנון חלק את הפרס עם המשוררת והמחזאית היהודייה נלי זקס, פליטה גרמנייה שנמלטה לשוודיה.
claims.quote: Agnon shared the $60,000 prize with Jewish poet and playwright Nelly Sachs, a German refugee who fled to Sweden.

claims.text: מלך שוודיה גוסטב השישי אדולף העניק את פרס נובל לספרות לשנת 1966 לשני הזוכים היהודים.
claims.quote: King Gustav VI Adolf, of Sweden, presented last night the 1966 Nobel Prize for Literature to the two Jewish co-winners

claims.text: בטקס ישב עגנון, ישראלי יליד גליציה, כשהוא חבוש כיפת קטיפה על בגדי הטקס הרשמיים.
claims.quote: Mr. Agnon, the Galician-born Israeli, wearing a velvet yarmulke atop his formal, white-tie attire

claims.text: בישראל נתפסה זכייתו של עגנון כהישג דיפלומטי גדול וכהזדמנות למדינה הצעירה למשוך תשומת לב כגורם תרבותי בעולם.
claims.quote: In Israel, Agnon’s award was viewed as a major diplomatic coup, and a ripe opportunity for the young state to gain attention as a cultural force on the world stage.

claims.text: עגנון, בן 78, כותב עברית, ונלי זקס, בת 75, כותבת גרמנית, והשניים חולקים את פרס נובל בסך 60,000 דולר.
claims.quote: Mr. Agnon, 78, writes in Hebrew; Miss Sachs, 75, writes in German. They share the $60,000 Nobel Prize award.

claims.text: מלבד פרס נובל זכה עגנון פעמיים בפרס ביאליק (1934 ו-1950) ופעמיים בפרס ישראל לספרות (1954 ו-1958).
claims.quote: Agnon was twice awarded both the Bialik Prize for literature (1934 and 1950) and the Israel Prize for literature (1954 and 1958).

claims.quote: Agnon remains Israel's sole literature laureate, canonized by the NIS 50 bill which bears his image alongside an excerpt of his Nobel Prize acceptance speech.

claims.quote: After his death and burial on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem

claims.text: זכרו של עגנון חי בשדרות שי עגנון בירושלים ובבית כנסת על שמו סמוך לביתו הישן בתלפיות.
claims.quote: His memory also lives on in Jerusalem's Sderot Shai Agnon, in a synagogue named after him a few blocks away from his old home in Talpiot

claims.text: בשנת 2007 נבחרה יצירתו של עגנון בין עשר היצירות החשובות בספרות העברית המודרנית.
claims.quote: In 2007, his work was named among the ten most important in modern Hebrew literature.

claims.text: לפי הרב סקס, עגנון לא היה מרוצה מהרעיון לחלוק את הפרס עם זקס.
claims.quote: The highly acclaimed author was not happy about the idea of sharing the prize with Sachs

claims.text: לפי הרב סקס, שר החוץ אבא אבן סבר שעליו לתרום לעיצוב נאומו של עגנון.
claims.quote: Abba Eban, then foreign minister of Israel, thought that he ought to have a hand in crafting Agnon’s speech

claims.text: לפי הרב סקס, מבחינה רטורית נוסח נאומו של עגנון מוזר בעליל.
claims.quote: As a piece of rhetoric, Agnon’s text is decidedly bizarre.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, חלק גדול מיצירתו של עגנון הפך לבלתי נגיש אפילו לקוראי עברית בישראל.
claims.quote: However, much of his work has become inaccessible, even to Hebrew readers in Israel

claims.text: לפי הרב סקס, ברשומות ההיסטוריות עגנון נולד בקיץ 1887.
claims.quote: It is a matter of historical record that he was born in the summer of 1887.

claims.text: לפי הרב סקס, עגנון טען שנולד בתשעה באב 1888, והטשטוש בשנת הלידה קשור כנראה לניסיונות להתחמק מגיוס.
claims.quote: This birth year obfuscation was likely related to draft-dodging efforts.

claims.text: לפי כתב העת AJS Review של הוצאת אוניברסיטת קיימברידג', באוקטובר 1912 עלה הסופר העברי שמואל יוסף עגנון, בן ה-24, על ספינה בנמל יפו בדרכו לברלין.
claims.quote: In October 1912, the twenty-four-year-old Hebrew writer Shmuel Yosef Agnon embarked on a ship in the port of Jaffa

claims.text: ב-6 ביוני 1924 פרצה שרפה בביתו בבאד הומבורג.
claims.quote: ב־6 ביוני 1924, כשנה לאחר מכן, פרצה דליקה בביתו של עגנון

claims.text: כל כתבי היד שלו ואוסף ספריו עלו באש.
claims.quote: In 1924 fire swept his home and destroyed all his books and manuscripts

claims.text: כל כתבי היד שלו ואוסף ספריו עלו באש.
claims.quote: האש כילתה את כתבי היד של עגנון

claims.text: עגנון היה לחתן פרס נובל הראשון של המדינה היהודית.
claims.quote: Agnon became Israel's first Nobel laureate when he received the literature prize in 1966.

claims.text: במאי 1967 יצא עגנון לסיור בארצות הברית.
claims.quote: It was May 23, 1967, just a few months after Agnon was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

claims.text: במאי 1967 יצא עגנון לסיור בארצות הברית.
claims.quote: in 1967 – on his first and only trip to America – Israeli author S.Y. Agnon stood before 1000 Americans

claims.text: לפי הארץ, עגנון הועמד לראשונה כמועמד לפרס נובל כבר ב-1947, אך זכה בפרס רק ב-1966.
claims.quote: had been formally suggested for the prize in 1947, 1949, 1951 and 1965
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: לפי הארץ, ההחלטה הסופית על הזכייה התקבלה ב-20 באוקטובר 1966, ובסיום הישיבה הודיע אוסטרלינג לעיתונאים על הזוכים
claims.quote: The final decision was made on October 20 by vote
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page
